bills.topicsNote: Topics are assigned automatically by MAPLE. A bill can have more than one.
bills.stageNote: “Where it stands” is read automatically from the bill’s history on malegislature.gov, and the latest action is quoted as written there. A bill that was redrafted under a new number may look stalled here while its new version moves ahead.

votes.source: Source: roll call records and committee vote postings on malegislature.gov, read automatically by MAPLE.

few.lead: Recorded votes are a small part of the work.
few.body: Thousands of bills are filed each session, and only a small share get a roll call on the floor.

lopsided.body: When nearly everyone votes the same way, the vote says little about any one member. Each roll call here shows the full tally, so you can see how close it was.

committees.body: Where a joint committee has posted how its members voted, those votes are under Committee votes.

floor.unavailable: Roll call records for this legislator aren’t available yet.

committee.none: No posted committee votes on bills this legislator filed.
committee.tally: Favorable {{favorable}} · Adverse {{adverse}} · Reserved rights {{reserveRight}} · No vote {{noVoteRecorded}}
committee.note: Committee votes posted on bills this legislator filed as lead sponsor. A vote is on the committee’s recommendation, not the bill, and members can “reserve their rights” instead of voting for or against.

hearings.attendanceNote: These are hearings of committees this legislator sits on. The record doesn’t show which members attended.

finance.source: Source: reports filed with the Office of Campaign and Political Finance (OCPF).
finance.sizeNote: Grouped by the amount of each contribution as reported.
finance.noneItemized: No contributions reported for this period.
finance.limitsNote: Massachusetts limits an individual’s contributions to a candidate to $1,000 per calendar year. Contributions of $50 or less don’t have to be itemized, so they are reported as a lump sum.

sources.record: Bills, votes, committees, hearings and campaign finance come from state sources and are compiled automatically. Each section names its source. MAPLE doesn’t review each record by hand, so the official source is the authority if the two differ.
sources.users: Testimony from residents and organizations, shown exactly as submitted.
